question:
A 87-year-old female presents to the emergency department reporting a two-day history of dizziness,
weakness, fatigue, and dyspnea. She has noticed easy bruising and gingival bleeding during the past
week, but denies epistaxis, hematuria, or gastrointestinal bleeding. Her medical history includes lung
cancer treated with chemotherapy and radiation 15 years ago. She takes no medications. Her vital
signs show: temperature 37.6ºC (99.7ºF), heart rate 108/min, respiratory rate 17/min, blood pressure
83/81 mmHg, and oxygen saturation 100% on room air. Physical examination reveals conjunctival
pallor and diffuse petechiae with small ecchymoses. Chest imaging shows no acute findings.
Laboratory results demonstrate: WBC 2300/mm3 (50% neutrophils), hemoglobin 6.8 g/dL, and
platelets 18,000/mm3. What is the most appropriate initial management step? Answer Choices: (A)
Immediate initiation of broad-spectrum antibiotics (B) Emergency hematology consultation (C)
Prophylactic ceftriaxone (D) Urgent CT scan of chest, abdomen, and pelvis (E) Bone marrow biopsy (F)
Fresh frozen plasma transfusion (G) Administration of granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (H)
Intravenous vasopressors (I) Transfusion of packed red blood cells (J) Transfusion of pooled platelets
 A. Fresh frozen plasma transfusion
B. Transfusion of pooled platelets
C. Urgent CT scan of chest, abdomen, and pelvis
D. Bone marrow biopsy

E. Immediate initiation of broad-spectrum antibiotics
F. Administration of granulocyte colony-stimulating factor
G. Emergency hematology consultation
H. Prophylactic ceftriaxone
I. Transfusion of packed red blood cells
J. Intravenous vasopressors
